release.title: Labour market statistics: June 2026 quarter
release.headline: The unemployment rate was 5.6 percent in the June 2026 quarter, compared with 5.4 percent in the March 2026 quarter.

executive_summary.text: The unemployment rate (HLFS, seasonally adjusted) was 5.6% in the June 2026 quarter, up from 5.4% in the March 2026 quarter (as revised in this release; first published as 5.3%).
The employment rate was 66.7% and the labour force participation rate 70.7% (seasonally adjusted). 2,905,000 people were employed and 171,000 were unemployed.
The underutilisation rate, a broader measure than unemployment, was 13.8%.

headline_metrics.label: Labour force participation rate (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)

context.text: Salary and wage rates (Labour Cost Index, all sectors) rose 0.6% in the quarter and 2.0% over the year to the June 2026 quarter. The LCI measures the price of labour for the same job; it is not average earnings.

previous_comparison.note: Rates are compared with earlier publications in the revisions table.

revisions.note: 2 of 161 quarters of the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate shared with Labour market statistics: March 2026 quarter were revised. Seasonal adjustment re-estimates history every quarter.

corrections.note: No earlier distinct statistical capture is stored for this publication.

definitions: The Household Labour Force Survey (HLFS) is a sample survey: its estimates have sampling error, and small quarterly movements may not be statistically significant. Stats NZ publishes sampling errors with each release.

The unemployment rate is unemployed people as a share of the labour force; the employment rate and the participation rate are shares of the working-age population (people aged 15 and over). The underutilisation rate is broader: it also counts people who want more hours and people who could work but are not looking or not yet available, as a share of the extended labour force.
notes: HLFS rates are seasonally adjusted and re-estimated every quarter, so earlier quarters can be revised. Where an earlier release is stored, the first-published figure is shown next to the latest.

The Labour Cost Index (LCI) measures changes in salary and wage rates for the same work of the same quality. The Quarterly Employment Survey (QES) measures average earnings, which also change with the mix of jobs and hours. They are different surveys and are not combined here; QES figures are not shown.
HLFS levels are published in thousands and rates to one decimal place.
This page describes published statistics only. It makes no forecast and no statement about policy.

series.name: Unemployment rate (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Unemployed people as a percentage of the labour force (employed plus unemployed). Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Employment rate (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Employed people as a percentage of the working-age population. Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Labour force participation rate (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: The labour force (employed plus unemployed) as a percentage of the working-age population. Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Underutilisation rate (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Underutilised people (unemployed, underemployed and the potential labour force) as a percentage of the extended labour force (labour force plus potential labour force). Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over. From March 2004.

series.name: Employed people (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Number of employed people, in thousands. Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Unemployed people (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Number of unemployed people (without work, available and actively seeking work), in thousands. Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Labour force (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: Employed plus unemployed people, in thousands. Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Working-age population (HLFS, seasonally adjusted)
series.definition: The usually resident, non-institutionalised civilian population aged 15 and over, in thousands. Household Labour Force Survey, seasonally adjusted, quarterly, people aged 15 and over.

series.name: Labour Cost Index, all salary and wage rates
series.definition: Labour Cost Index, all salary and wage rates (including overtime), all sectors combined, all industries; base June 2009 quarter (=1000). Measures the change in the price of labour for the same work of the same quality; it is not average earnings (that is the Quarterly Employment Survey). Not seasonally adjusted.

series.name: Labour Cost Index, quarterly change
series.definition: Percentage change in the Labour Cost Index (all salary and wage rates, all sectors) from the previous quarter, as published by Stats NZ (1 d.p.). Not seasonally adjusted.

series.name: Labour Cost Index, annual change
series.definition: Percentage change in the Labour Cost Index (all salary and wage rates, all sectors) from the same quarter a year earlier, as published by Stats NZ (1 d.p.).

revisions.note: First published: the figure in the release for that quarter. Where that release is not stored, the earliest stored figure is shown and marked as earliest stored. Latest: Labour market statistics: June 2026 quarter.
